history.summary: CSV town 'Kota' is CORRECT - the documented referent is the Godavari Dham Balaji Temple on Rawatbhata Road, Dadabari/Shivpura, Kota (324009), on the banks of the Chambal river. It is a modern Hanuman (Balaji) temple - the local name 'Balaji' here denotes Hanuman - known for its serene riverside setting and its special morning and midnight aarti on Tuesdays and Saturdays. The complex also houses shrines of Shiva, Bhairav and Ganpati, plus a gaushala and prasad shops, and is considered one of Kota's oldest and most-visited Hanuman temples. CONFLICT FLAG: one travel source (Zee Zest) describes Godavari Dham as 'dedicated to Lord Shiva and Lady Parvati, constructed in the form of a huge shivling' - this contradicts all Kota-specific listings and reviews, which describe a Hanuman temple; treat the Zee Zest claim as a likely conflation with a different Godavari Dham and do not merge. NAME COLLISION FLAG: there is a second, unrelated 'Godavari Dham Temple' at Atru Tehsil, Baran district, Rajasthan (~89 km from Kota) - the two should not be mixed. The temple is named for the sacred Godavari river, symbolising purity.
